title: Bogduk 1992: moment arm of psoas major at L3-L4 (M, radiograph_flexed)
muscle_as_reported: psoas major fascicles (origin: vertebral body VB, transverse process TP, intervertebral disc IVD)

imaging.modality: lateral radiographs (magnification corrected x1/1.62) with fascicle lines constructed from cadaver anatomy
imaging.level_definition: instantaneous axis of rotation of each lumbar motion segment

quantity.name: moment_arm
quantity.definition: true moment arm: perpendicular distance from the joint/segment rotation axis (or instantaneous axis) to the muscle line of action; sagittal-plane flexion(+)/extension(-) moment arm: perpendicular distance from the fascicle line of action to the instantaneous axis of rotation (IAR) of the segment, on radiograph tracings

source.authors: Bogduk N, Pearcy M, Hadfield G
source.sample: 10 adult males (radiographs) + 3 cadavers (6 psoas muscles); lateral flexion-extension radiographs of 10 adult males; fascicle anatomy from dissection of 3 embalmed cadavers

how_to_simulate: Pose the model lumbar spine in full lumbar flexion (no hip flexion) (match the radiographic posture; no hip flexion in flexed/extended).

For each psoas fascicle crossing L3-L4, compute the sagittal moment arm about the L3-L4 axis of rotation (IAR; if the model uses a fixed joint centre, use it and note the difference) = -dL/dtheta or the perpendicular distance.
Sign: + flexion (fascicle anterior to the axis), - extension. Compare each fascicle with mean ± SD (n=10).
protocol.notes: True moment arms (geometric, about the segmental IAR). Moments in the table (multiples of K) are derived and not stored. Fascicle line-of-action orientation (Tables 4, 6, 8) not stored.

extraction.check_notes: All Ma/SD cells read from the rendered Table 5 (pp.114-117); text layer misaligned the L5-S1 column.
